page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7nex.large is a compute-optimized Virtual Private Cloud instance within the ecs.c7nex family. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz, this instance features 1 physical core supporting 2 vCPUs via hyper-threading. It is provisioned with 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a 48 MB L3 cache, alongside specialized instruction sets including AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI. The instance operates without attached local NVMe storage and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps on a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals moderate single-thread efficiency alongside limited parallel execution capabilities due to its 2-vCPU hardware footprint. Single-core tests such as stress-ng (1847.58) and Geekbench single-core (1500.0) place within average performance distributions, while gzip compression reaches 27.77 GB/sec. However, multi-core benchmarks show constrained output, registering a stress-ng multi-core score of 1930.87 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1751.0, both falling into lower tier percentiles. Memory bandwidth throughput remains restricted, measured at 14.01 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 12.76 GB/sec for writes.

From a workload evaluation perspective, the instance provides entry-level compute resources with a low memory footprint per core. The absence of local disk storage requires network-attached volume provisioning for stateful applications. While multi-threaded database tasks (977.34 operations/sec in PassMark) and heavy parallel compilations show performance bottlenecks, the instance maintains adequate throughput for lightweight web microservices, single-threaded batch processing, and lightweight utility services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7nex.large is a compute-oriented instance powered by a dedicated 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor configured with 1 physical core, 2 vCPUs, and 4.0 GB of RAM. Running on a KVM hypervisor, it includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 extensions, while providing a 3 Gbps baseline network capacity without local storage. Performance benchmarks demonstrate average single-threaded capability, evidenced by a 1500.0 Geekbench single-core score and 27.77 GB/sec gzip compression. Conversely, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics reflect hardware limitations, with multi-threaded stress-ng achieving 1930.87 and uncached read bandwidth reaching 14.01 GB/sec. Given its low vCPU count and dedicated resource allocation, this instance represents a budget-conscious option for single-threaded utilities, lightweight web serving, and basic microservice hosting rather than memory-intensive or heavily parallel workloads.
